children: British wages, excluding bonuses, grew by 3.5% in the three months to July compared with the same period in 2025, official data showed on Tuesday.
Economists polled by Reuters had mostly expected regular wage growth of 3.5%.
The Bank of England is trying to gauge whether higher energy prices caused by the Iran war will interrupt a gradual cooling of wage growth and underlying inflation pressure in Britain.

Investors on Monday were pricing a roughly one-in-three chance of a quarter-point interest rate hike by the BoE on Thursday. A rate hike at the following Monetary Policy Committee meeting in November was seen as almost certain followed by another in December.
